_readme: Persistent fetch-failure ledger for the Las Azules S2 media sweep routine. Sweeps must read this before attempting any body fetch on a candidate URL and skip anything currently in cooldown, rendering the skip on the sweep evidence line. failCount tracks consecutive full fallback-chain failures (WebFetch AND Firecrawl scrape both failed in the same attempt). Three consecutive full-chain failures sets cooldownUntil to 30 days out. After cooldown expires, the URL gets one retry (WebFetch then Firecrawl); success resets failCount to 0 and clears cooldownUntil, failure restarts the 30-day cooldown. A separate category, permanentSkip with a skipReason, marks URLs that are fetchable but excluded for an editorial reason (for example a syndicated republication of a story already in data.json under a primary outlet). permanentSkip entries are skipped regardless of cooldownUntil and must never be treated as, or logged as, a fetch failure. See LEMA-9620 for origin, LEMA-9619 for the incident that motivated this file, and LEMA-9621 for the permanentSkip category.

entries.skipNote: Syndicated Variety wire story ('Women in Blue' Renewed for Season 2 at Apple TV+, byline Joe Otterson, dated 2025-05-20) republished by IMDb news. The same renewal announcement is already present in data.json from the Variety original (https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/women-in-blue-renewed-season-2-apple-tv-1236404908/) plus 15 other outlets covering the same event. Not a fetch failure, the URL is fetchable via the Firecrawl fallback (see history). Excluded on editorial grounds: adding it would be a duplicate-story entry, not new coverage. See LEMA-9621.

history.note: Fallback chain resolved it. Firecrawl returned the real article body (a syndicated Variety renewal story, byline Joe Otterson, dated 2025-05-20). WebFetch alone still fails (403/202 zero-byte bot wall) but the standing fallback now succeeds, so this URL is not placed in cooldown. See LEMA-9620 deliverable for the decision reasoning.

Retry succeeded: WebFetch returned real post content this time (cast meeting original female police officers), not the empty bot-wall body seen previously. Ledger reset per fallback-chain success rule. Not added to data.json this run: no publish date could be located anywhere in the fetched body or via corroborating search, and the schema requires a real ts/date -- fabricating one would violate the no-fabrication guardrail. Candidate remains available for a future run if a dateable source (e.g. a news pickup citing this post) surfaces.
